$comment: 07_DOMAIN_AND_STATE_MACHINES 'Platform topology': dependencies flow from contracts to domain ports, application orchestration and concrete adapters; UI consumes HTTP DTOs; the cores do not depend on persistence, payments, framework or UI. Every workspace package must be assigned a layer here; tools/architecture-gate.mjs enforces the allowed edges, forbids deep/private/sibling imports, cycles, and server-only code or credentials in client bundles. A test-only subpath (testOnlySubpaths) may be imported only from a package's test/ directory, never from production source, so no deployment import graph carries test code; a workspace dependency a package declares but never imports is refused, because an unused edge still ships and installs with the package.
$commentClientBundles: B11 design D-SEC-2. clientBundleNodeSide lists, relative to a client-bundle package, the files that never ship to a browser (tests, build scripts and configuration, the browser-test harness): the client-bundle rules do not apply to them, the layer rules still do. A client bundle may not declare a Server Action or a server data cache, and may not import a module forbiddenInClientBundles names.
$commentServerConfig: B11 design D-SEC-2. Every file of a client-bundle package that reads the environment (process.env, import.meta.env) lives in one of serverConfigDirectories and starts with the serverOnlyImport line, so the bundler refuses to put it in a browser bundle; the pure modules beside it take their values as arguments and stay importable by node:test.
$commentRawCores: B05 D5-1/D5-6 (S046). Each vendored core (a pinned tarball under vendor/) is importable only by its wrapper package, at the root; the wrapper re-exports the core's root API and nothing else. rawCoreForbiddenSubpaths are never imported by production source, not even by the wrapper (the IC campaign surface).
